findings.source_passage: this is marvellous, sometimes most comical. Wherefore this difference? A problem? Perhaps not.
findings.source_locator: paragraph 4, transition into the Belshazzar digression
findings.why_it_matters: The source's rhetorical staging — 'this is marvellous, sometimes most comical' — is part of the narrator's ironic voice and sets up the Belshazzar digression; the draft omits these transitional exclamations and jumps straight to the problem-posing, losing the comedic register.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'this is marvellous, sometimes most comical' before 'Wherefore this difference?' to preserve the narrator's ironic comic tone.

findings.source_passage: the mate received his meat as though receiving alms; and cut it tenderly; and a little started if, perchance, the knife grazed against the plate; and chewed it noiselessly; and swallowed it, not without circumspection.
findings.why_it_matters: The anaphoric 'and…and…and' rhythm is signature Melville periodic prose; the draft condenses it into three quick clauses and drops 'swallowed it, not without circumspection,' losing the comedic solemnity that makes the passage memorable.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the full anaphoric chain, including 'swallowed it, not without circumspection,' to preserve the rhythmic signature.

findings.source_passage: What a relief it was to choking Stubb, when a rat made a sudden racket in the hold below.
findings.source_locator: paragraph 5, after 'Ahab forbade not conversation; only he himself was dumb'
findings.why_it_matters: This is a tonally distinctive comic beat — the rat as Stubb's savior — that punctuates the oppressive silence at table. Its absence removes a well-known piece of Melvillean comic relief that many readers remember.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the rat sentence after 'only he was dumb' to preserve the comic relief and voice.

findings.source_passage: for when they did enter it, it was something as a street-door enters a house; turning inwards for a moment, only to be turned out the next
findings.source_locator: final paragraph, on mates and harpooneers 'living out of the cabin'
findings.why_it_matters: The street-door simile is a small but characteristically Melvillean conceit that gives the observation rhetorical texture; without it the statement is merely factual.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the street-door simile to retain the narrator's analogical playfulness.

summary: The draft preserves the chapter's major signatures — the Belshazzar passage verbatim, Flask's butterless fate, the Daggoo/Dough-Boy scalping scene, the closing Bear/Logan/paws paragraph — but flattens three voice-defining passages (Starbuck's anaphoric alms-eating, the rat-in-the-hold comic beat, and the transitional 'marvellous, most comical') at medium severity, falling just short of the regeneration threshold.
